To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the incentive compatibility of a settlement mechanism depends on: (1) the degree to which the mechanism allows the risk to be shared among the parties; (2) the degree to and the manner in which the mechanism allows a party to share the settlement risk with other parties; and (3) the degree to, the manner in, and the extent to which the mechanism uses the risk-sharing information in the settlement decision.

the incentive compatibility constraints in a settlement mechanism are such that the risk exposure of a party to a settlement risk is a function of its private information, and that the risk exposure is increasing in the riskiness of the transfers being made.
the incentive compatible risk-sharing scheme that is most efficient is a linear scheme, and that the optimal linear scheme is the one in which the third party bears all of the settlement risk.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question.
the design of a settlement mechanism in which the risk of settlement failure is shared among the parties in the network in a manner which is incentive efficient and incentive compatible.
the design of incentive efficient risk-sharing mechanisms in a settlement arrangement, where a third party possesses some information that is private to it.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the third party is better off by revealing its private information to the network.
the settlement arrangement is not incentive compatible, and the third party will not reveal its private information.

in the class of environments considered in this paper, a third-party clearing agent that is exposed to the settlement risk is not able to provide a more accurate estimate of the riskiness of the payment than the parties that are making the payment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the settlement risk can be used by the clearinghouse as an incentive device to elicit the private information from the participants.
the third party's incentive to provide the best possible information about the risk of a transaction depends on its own risk exposure to the transaction.
, in the absence of an information revelation mechanism, a third party would be motivated to provide a biased report on the riskiness of payments being made.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a third party may be induced to provide information that is of value to the other parties in the network, and that this information may improve the efficiency of the settlement arrangement.
, in a settlement mechanism, the incentive to share information is enhanced if the third party is exposed to the settlement risk.
the exposure to settlement risk can be used as a means to incentivize a third party to reveal information that is useful in managing settlement risk.
